newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crude prices steady in Asia, wet barrels quiet.
newsitem.headline: Crude prices steady in Asia, wet barrels quiet.

text.p: Crude oil prices rose in Asia on Monday, extending gains made in overseas markets on Friday, while the wet market was quiet with trading in most Middle East cargoes for November nearing its close, traders said.

Most market participants attributed the jump in oil prices to news that Kurdish fighters from the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) retook their stronghold Sulaimaniya in northern Iraq from a rival group.
At 0835 GMT, November NYMEX light crude on the ACCESS after-hours system was indicated at $24.95/25.01, up from the contract's close in New York of $24.66 on Friday.
The November contract had gained 40 cents in New York.
On SIMEX, November Brent was bid at $24.25 and offered at $24.30, compared with the contract's close at $23.98 on the IPE on Friday.

Brent/Dubai spreads were a touch wider than late overseas levels due to Brent's gains. December Brent/Dubai was notionally assessed at $2.30/2.35 and January Brent/Dubai was notionally assessed at $2.15/2.20.
In the wet market, a few November Oman cargoes appeared to be available in the market.

However, it was unclear if there were still buyers for the cargoes. The level for November Oman was assessed at between parity to MPM and MPM plus five cents. A November Masila was rumoured to have been sold last week to a major.
Traders said discussion in December light Middle East crudes was likely to start this week, but firm indications could not yet be heard.

In regional crudes, November Tapis was bid/offered at $25.40/25.50, a trader said. He said Minas was attracting a bid of ICP plus 20 cents and an offer of ICP plus 30 cents.--M.Yoshikawa/Tokyo (+813 5473 3706)/N.Fullick/Sinagpore.
